title: Martin Casado on the Demand Forces Behind AI

reader_summary.headline: What's gonna happen to central buyers and platform teams and IT teams if agents are making the decision?
reader_summary.overview: What's gonna happen to central buyers and platform teams and IT teams if agents are making the decision? It's very clear that coding is pretty much dead but engineering is very much not. Every time you have a technical epoch you have to redo everything and we forget that every time.

key_points.text: I don't think people even have a common definition of a bubble.
key_points.evidence_quote: I don't think people even have a common definition of a bubble.

key_points.text: If AI demand is real and accelerating why does everything still feel constrained?
key_points.evidence_quote: If AI demand is real and accelerating why does everything still feel constrained?

key_points.text: Why does a technology that's clearly delivering value also feel harder to scale and expect it?
key_points.evidence_quote: Why does a technology that's clearly delivering value also feel harder to scale and expect it?

key_points.text: In early technology shifts it was easy to assume the hard problems were solved.
key_points.evidence_quote: In early technology shifts it was easy to assume the hard problems were solved.

thesis: The discussion argues that while AI demand is real and accelerating with genuine productivity gains, the market faces a supply underhang rather than a bubble, causing constraints in power, physical footprint, and coordination. It posits that every technical epoch requires rebuilding the entire stack, meaning infrastructure has moved back to the center of the story as the primary bottleneck outside the models themselves.
